history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: This temple is NOT in Kamalpur (a Dhalai-district town) - the CSV town is WRONG. The Kasba Kali Temple is at Kasba village by Kamalasagar lake, Bishalgarh subdivision, Sipahijala district, ~27 km south of Agartala, directly on the India-Bangladesh border. Built on a hilltop by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in the late 15th century; the Kamalasagar lake in front was dug by him (1490-1520) and named after his wife Kamala Devi. The presiding idol, Kasbeswari Kali, is a 15th-century sandstone Mahishasurmardini (Dasabhuja Durga) worshipped as Kali, with a Shivalinga at her feet; the present structure dates to the 17th century. An Indo-Bangla border hut nearby is a local attraction. Note: 'Kasba' is a Farsi term for town; the area was earlier known as Kamalagarh/Koilagarh. town_description: Kasba is a border village in Sipahijala district ~27 km south of Agartala, named from the Farsi 'kasba' meaning town (earlier known as Kamalagarh/Koilagarh). It centres on the 15th-century Kamalasagar lake and the hilltop Kasba Kali Bari overlooking it, sitting right beside the India-Bangladesh border fence with an Indo-Bangla border hut nearby.
